clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old female presented in mid-2014 with strong pain in her left iliac region. Initial workup included endovaginal pelvic ultrasonography (September 2014) showing an enlarged left ovary with a cyst, normal tumor markers (October 2014), and MRI suggesting an enlarged left ovary where neoplasia could not be excluded. Given her history of bathing in rivers in schistosomiasis-endemic areas, a left ovariectomy was performed. Histopathological examination of the removed ovarian tissue (April 2015) definitively identified ovarian schistosomiasis, characterized by granulomatous inflammatory processes surrounding viable and calcified S. mansoni eggs, and explicitly ruled out neoplastic tissue. Macroscopic and microscopic examination of the resected ovary further detailed the pathological findings. Follow-up in April 2016 showed the patient in good general condition with normal abdominal ultrasound findings, but also revealed a residual S. mansoni infection through parasitological feces examinations.
